# Secrets from Environment Only

Credentials are read from environment variables and from nowhere else, and `.gitignore` is written so
that the lazy path and the safe path are the same path.

> "**Credentials come from the environment.** Nothing resembling a secret belongs in a tracked file,
> and `.gitignore` covers `.env` and key material so that staying honest is the path of least
> resistance."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/labs/10_web_scraping_and_email/README.md, 2026-07-25

The second clause is the whole design. Discipline that depends on remembering fails; discipline
enforced by the ignore rules does not. `.env`, `*.pem` and `*.key` are ignored, so the file a
developer would naturally create is one git will not offer to stage.

## What lab 10 does with it

An SMTP + REST + scraping lab in [[python-programming-laboratories]] — the one place in either
repository that handles real credentials. Three hardening choices sit beside the env-var rule:

- **`EmailMessage` rather than string-formatted headers.** Building a message by concatenation lets a
  newline in a user-supplied subject inject arbitrary headers — a Bcc, a spoofed From. Using the
  email API makes header injection structurally impossible instead of filtered.
- **`starttls(context=ssl.create_default_context())`.** The default context verifies the certificate
  and the hostname. `starttls()` with no context is the version that appears in most tutorials and
  the version that accepts any certificate.
- **`timeout=` on every request**, so a hung endpoint fails rather than blocks forever.

## Scope — do not overstate it

This is what the repository does, and it is the correct baseline. It is **not** a secrets-management
practice: there is no vault, no key rotation, no CI secret store, and no CI at all. **TODO:** whether
"basic operational security" in the README's skills list means anything beyond env vars, `.gitignore`
and the TLS context is unconfirmed; `confidence: low` on any wider claim.

Nothing resembling a credential was found in either lab repository during recon — the pattern holds
in practice, not only in prose. Note that the same repo commits a **stale personal absolute path** in
`lab6_Neo4j/guide.txt` over in [[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]]: not a secret, but the same class
of local-machine detail leaking into a tracked file. See [[documentation-drift]].
